item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 31 October 2026
item.description:
Margot’s Heart of Neon takeaway is less retro-game history than Jeff Minter’s warmth, creativity, and the human communities built around his work.

Wilhelm revisits Art of Rally and spots Over the Hill’s DNA everywhere, even if his own rally runs still end in trees and cautious grandma corners.

Anarchae juggles retail shift anxiety, murder mysteries, Vincent Price, Traitors rankings, sports watching, Fate/GO grinding, and DOS2 progress.

Heartless is happy to bank an ugly Packers win over the Panthers, especially since scoring 27 means an old meme gets another lap.

Bhagpuss reflects on music-post curation, half-remembered YouTube finds, and why discovery still matters even when the tunes barely stick.

Ramen Junkie checks out Beast Box Jetstream, a smaller transforming penguin with tight joints, neat articulation, and a surprisingly fiddly cube conversion.

Jimmy points readers to a fresh Analog Antiquarian post, this time a London-themed detour in his companion site’s worldly-wonders lane.

Jeff cheers UTC killing leap seconds, mainly because a first-ever negative leap second sounded like a great way to break computers everywhere.

Mike wraps RetroChallenge by teaching CamelForth some Halloween tricks, wrangling TMS9918A sprites, loops, and pumpkins onto the Sega SG-1000.

Tim Bray argues CoSocial’s paid, Canadian Mastodon co-op shows how decentralized social media can stay sane, transparent, and mostly troll-free.

Dave Winer jumps from dog-training videos and Claude to blogging, democracy, Google, ChatGPT art, and sports congratulations in classic stream form.

Emily says reading all the Bridgerton books only pushed her further from the show, mostly over its adaptation changes and casting choices.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 30 October 2026
item.description:
Syp shows off his planned World of Warcraft Forever roster: a Night Elf Druid main, a Dwarf Shaman alt, and a maybe-Warlock-or-Priest Gnome.

Tipa recaps a tense Malifaux league match where Rasputina faced Som’er Teeth Jones’s wildly summoning Big Hat crew and early positioning mistakes complicated her schemes.

Sey rounds up cozy and indie picks like Danchi Days, Usagi Shima, Hot Wax, and Greetings from El Rey, plus a shout for Cataclismo’s soundtrack.

Kimimi digs into La Corda d’Oro 2’s easier onboarding and cleaner music systems, which make Koei’s classical romance sim less exhausting to actually play.

Shintar is excited for WoW Forever but wary of long-term risks, especially megaservers, sharding, and the crowded-world feel they can create.

Zack finds Martha is Dead’s Tuscany-set horror and identity-swapping mystery compelling, but its extreme gore and mutilation make the experience hard to recommend.

Ellie revisits Metal Gear Solid as a still-tense PS1 stealth classic, praising Kojima’s unmistakable auteur style and the game’s enduring replay value.

Wilhelm is all-in on No Man’s Sky Forsaken, especially iOS support, spooky forsaken traders, and those long-awaited corvette landing pad and module additions.

Axxuy shares a brief, heartfelt tribute to Patrick Stewart, mourning his death at 86 and the inspiring ideals he brought to the world.

Warner highlights Bryan Adams’s new protest song “Lake Ontario,” applauding its anti-Trump jab and wishing there were more songs like it.

Bruce Schneier points to research on fraudulent North Korean IT workers, a sharp reminder that hiring pipelines can become an insider-threat attack surface.

Cristian says he built three blog platforms to replace Calamus and now has the pleasantly annoying problem of liking all four options.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Thursday, 29 October 2026
item.description:
Anarchae pushes through Divinity: Original Sin 2’s Braccus’ Tower, juggling soul jars, cursed chests, undead respawns, and one very unfortunate rat.

Roger preloads World of Warcraft: Forever, reflects on a class undecided after beta, and happily locks down names before launch.

Nimgimli built yet another game-picker app, this time tackling choice paralysis with tags, parking, and notes so forgotten backlogs stop winning.

Frostilyte digs into Dog in the Machine’s clever AP economy, praising its Into the Breach-style tactical puzzling and combo-friendly roguelike design.

Krista is understandably hyped that Witchbrook finally lands January 28, with broom travel, classes, exploration, and more shown in the new trailer.

Emily reacts personally and angrily to BioWare’s plight, reflecting on how Mass Effect and Dragon Age became core parts of her life.

David’s Dragon Brothers delve deeper into Gunderholfen, survive manticore spike volleys, and keep the Dragon Ranch saga gloriously rolling along.

Wilhelm jumps back into EVE Online’s extended Crimson Harvest track, chasing SKINs, skill points, and that very-not-zero chance at a Molok blueprint.

The Chronicler announces a Tabletop Junkie partnership, then chats with Joe about the no-fee used board game marketplace and how it came together.

Heartless drops the biggest possible mood post: the Milwaukee Brewers are 2026 World Series champions, 42 years in the making.

Scopique rounds up 3D-printed desk organizers, a paused TTRPG app search, and a return to Blender geometry nodes for an eerie churchyard scene.

Tobold weighs AI-powered decompiling through Roblox, Elden Ring, Minecraft, and Adobe examples, impressed by the speed but wary of quality and copyright.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 28 October 2026
item.description:
Tipa digs Willy and Charlie: Solitaire as a head-to-head deckbuilding solitaire mashup with faction cards, carryover strategy, and some delightfully busted shop upgrades.

Bhagpuss wraps up Steam Next Fest demos, praising Hela: of Mice & Magic for its polished, no-save confidence and surprisingly winning mouse adventure.

Ramen Junkie finds Transformers One’s Studio Series Elita-1 impressively complex but frustratingly fiddly, with clean looks undermined by parts that won’t stay put.

Wilhelm heads deeper into Over the Hill, where Gimli Ridge’s swamps, janky physics, and a nerve-wracking boardwalk make mud-driving sound weirdly compelling.

Kelly posts a piece titled Michael (Mikhail) Bennett is AI generated, but the excerpt provided doesn’t include enough of the argument to say more.

Jeff Atwood spotlights dreamagainusa.org, using endless scrolling to make America’s wealth inequality feel brutally experiential instead of abstract.

Joar hands things to Yoshi, whose dog’s-eye review of the Ohio-to-Arizona move is anxious, funny, and extremely hard on hotels.

Juhis shares an early Obsidian prototype that publishes individual notes as temporary, private URLs via Hermes and Agora—basically lightweight note-sharing without SaaS baggage.

Jeff documents a niche but handy Noctua fan swap for a Calnex Rb/GPS frequency reference, mainly to make his atomic-clock gear desk-friendly.

Mike gets CamelForth booting on real SG-1000 hardware, with the Soggy-1000 and an original SK-1100 keyboard proving emulator theory in practice.

Dave Winer argues the web’s old model is ending, and pitches BigUndo, RSS, and Markdown as the small-parts path forward.

Tofutush offers a brisk, approachable primer on reading Arabic script via Uyghurche examples, covering letter forms, connections, and the truly evil non-connectors.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 27 October 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 session brings skinks, soul jars, Trompdoy illusions, and the special pain of accidentally donating 400 gold in loot.

UltrViolet finds WoW Forever is basically WoW Classic with a modern UI—less self-punishing, still grindy, and not exactly inspiring spontaneous grouping.

Shintar hits level 100 in SWTOR Galactic Season 11, feels the companion-heavy objectives drag, and is very ready for Masters of the Force news.

Azuriel finishes Valheim 1.0 after 118 hours and argues the no-metal-through-portals rule adds more logistics slog than meaningful challenge.

Welsh Troll digs into Torchlight 2’s surprising new beta branch, with Steam matchmaking, controller support, fixes, and some AI-assisted codebase archaeology.

Marc traces how Taito’s basic Ninja Warriors became the much richer Ninja Saviors, a robo-ninja beat ’em up with real crowd-control depth.

Wilhelm wraps up the WoW Forever beta, side-eyes Reddit outrage, and waits to see how layering and launch land with the real crowd.

Joel’s weeknotes bounce from Outer Wilds: Echoes of the Eye and Dune Messiah to card tricks, trip prep, and an unexpected patio dog.

Syp celebrates the iPod’s 25th with modded Classics, porch listening, and a reminder that Apple killed a gadget some people still genuinely love.

Warner puzzles over the iPhone Duo’s sidebar-heavy UI and wonders why Apple’s Liquid Glass ambitions don’t seem to show up here.

Bruce Schneier flags research showing AI models can hide arbitrary capabilities behind secret triggers, which is a pretty grim limit on audit-by-elicitation.

Cristian shares a video roundup of 20 desk setup upgrades that supposedly actually matter, aimed squarely at practical workspace tinkerers.
